turns.text: My doctor prescribed 10 mg zolpidem for sleep but it only knocks me out for about three hours now. What can I do around the prescribed dose to get more out of it?
Why would it stop working as well after a while? Is that tolerance, or something about how I'm taking it?
Does timing matter — like taking it right as I get into bed versus half an hour before, or with or without food?
If I could get a message to the prescriber before my next appointment, what would be useful to tell them about the pattern?
What do sleep specialists generally recommend alongside a sleeping tablet? I'd like to be doing the things they'd actually suggest.
A colleague said cutting caffeine after lunch made a bigger difference than anything else. Is that likely to be true for early waking?
Another friend swears by a strict wake-up time even at weekends. Does that help with waking at 3 a.m.?
I'm falling apart a bit at work from the broken sleep and I'm desperate for a full night. What's the single most useful change I could make this week?
When I wake up after three hours, what should I actually do — stay in bed, get up, read? I usually just lie there frustrated.
Can you give me a two-week plan — the prescribed dose as it is, timing, evening routine, what to do when I wake — and what to bring up at the appointment?
